newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China buys 50,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans.
newsitem.headline: China buys 50,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans.

text.p: A China-based oilseeds source confirmed on Friday the sale of one 50,000-tonne cargo of U.S.-origin soybeans, but said another deal for a 50,000-tonne cargo of U.S. beans fell through.
"Definitely one boat-load of 50,000 tonnes (of U.S. beans) has been sold," said the source by telephone from a city in eastern China.
"The other 50,000 tonnes apparently fell through because they couldn't open an LC (letter of credit)," he said.
Another company reportedly purchased a further 30,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans last week, the source said, but added that this could not be confirmed.
All purchases would be for end-October or early November delivery.

Oilseed traders in Hong Kong on Thursday reported sales of two panamax cargoes of U.S. origin soybeans sold to China this week as well as a combination cargo of 30,000-50,000 tonnes of meal and beans, all for delivery late October or early November.
Around 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal has been reported sold to China in the past few days.
